content.name: On-Demand Webinar: Sensor Measurements 101
content.linkedin_copy:

content.name: How Will Test and Measurement Evolve in the New Year?
content.linkedin_copy:
Test and measurement for critical infrastructure is entering a new phase. In 2026, changes that have been emerging in the background are set to shift to become front of mind.

These changes relate to security, AI, photonics and sensing. While all could be said to be related but evolving independently, they are now converging to directly affect one another. This convergence categorically changes how we need to develop, roll out and test the networks, data centers and critical infrastructure they run on.

In this blog, VIAVI CTO Sameh Yamany outlines his big five predictions for the year ahead: https://blog.viavisolutions.com/2026/01/13/how-will-test-and-measurement-evolve-in-the-new-year/

content.name: On-Demand Webinar: Clocks and Serial Data Signal Integrity for System Development
content.linkedin_copy:
Designing high-speed links? As clock and data rates climb, signal integrity is critical for reliable performance.
In this on-demand webinar, Dallas Mohler, Senior Applications Engineer at Tektronix, shares a repeatable workflow to quickly observe and debug real-world SerDes issues—closed eye diagrams, excessive jitter, unexpected noise, and confusing results.
You’ll learn:
Where and how to probe signals for meaningful insight.
How to set up clock recovery and when to apply equalization (CTLE/DFE)
Methodologies to address closed eyes, random vs deterministic jitter, channel & signal path effects, and power rail induced noise
Spot and solve SerDes signal integrity issues fast with fewer re-spins and faster bring-up.

content.name: Blog: New De-embedding, Embedding, and Equalization Software for High-Speed Systems Verification and Compliance Test
content.linkedin_copy:
From multi-gigabit serial designs like PCIe, DDR5, USB4, and multi-lane Ethernet to cutting-edge RF and power electronics, Tektronix Signal Integrity Modeling (SIM) helps ensure your design meets both compliance and real-world performance requirements.
By removing and simulating reflections, loss, and delay from cables, components, and fixtures, SIM eliminates two common traps in validation—false failures and false confidence—so results reflect your device, not your setup.
In this post, see how SIM—available for the 5 and 6 Series B MSOs and the new 7 Series DPO—lets you de-embed, embed, apply equalization, visualize signals anywhere, and compare “what‑if” scenarios directly on your oscilloscope to validate standards compliance and real-world performance faster.

content.name: Electrification of Aviation [EA Bidirectional Power Supplies]
content.linkedin_copy:
Air traffic contributes up to 3.1% of global CO₂ emissions, a figure expected to triple by 2050 without effective countermeasures. To address this, the German Research Foundation (DFG) funded the SE²A Cluster of Excellence to develop a climate-neutral air transport system. The future of flight is electric, but transitioning to electric propulsion comes with significant technical hurdles, such as managing highly dynamic voltage transients and integrating advanced power-electronic topologies.
Together with equipment from EA Elektro-Automatik, Tektronix supports the E²AGLE research project, which is developing next-generation electric propulsion systems for aircraft. Precise measurement and test solutions ensure reliable results even at high voltages and during dynamic transients.
Read the story to discover how Tektronix is accelerating climate-neutral aircraft propulsion—and how it can inspire and advance your projects.
https://www.tek.com/en/stories/tektronix-supports-the-electrification-of-aviation?utm_source=msdm&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ea-psb-story|en#_msdynmkt_donottrack=0,_msdynmkt_linkid=21b017ab-e108-43e8-ae87-4f623af50671

content.name: Hyperloop Story
content.linkedin_copy:
For years now, the transportation industry has consisted of four modes of transportation—cars, trains, boats, and airplanes. In 2013, the Hyperloop—a conceptual high-speed transportation system in which pressurized vehicles travel through near-vacuum tubes—was introduced. 
Delft Hyperloop’s latest pod, DH09 “THEIA,” is on a mission to develop a climate-neutral, scalable hyperloop system and to become the fifth mode of transportation. 
Read the full story to see how the 2 Series MSO helped the team accelerate testing of THEIA’s propulsion and levitation. https://www.tek.com/en/stories/delft-hyperloop-customer-story

content.name: Engineering Fundamentals 101 | On-Demand Webinar
content.linkedin_copy:
Discover the importance of the I-V characteristic curve, a graphical representation of current (I) and power as a function of voltage (V), widely used for characterizing electronic devices.
Join Keithley Application Engineer Liz Makley as she demystifies the I-V curve and its significance in understanding device behavior, performance, and reliability. Through real-world test setups, Liz will demonstrate how to generate an I-V curve, interpret its shape, characteristics, and provide valuable insights into the electrical properties of devices like semiconductor MOSFETs and diodes. She'll also share pro tips for I-V characterization.
Watch this on-demand webinar to gain a solid foundation in basic characteristics and be equipped to tackle more complex tests in the future.
https://tek.brandlive.com/Measurements-101/en/session/b6e9d2ca-71b3-11f0-b254-a7b3a99bc2cb

content.name: Multichannel, Mixed Domain Analysis
content.linkedin_copy:
If you are an engineer developing today’s systems with multiple RF interfaces or complex embedded synthesizer or other RF functions, you will want to see how you can benefit from multi-channel, mixed domain signal acquisition and analysis to measure, and interpret signals across multiple channels, frequencies, and time intervals.

Discover how you can unlock exciting capabilities using hardware digital downconverters (DDCs) in parallel with time domain signal processing.
 
View any analog channel as a waveform, spectrum, or both
Plot and trigger on changes in RF frequency or magnitude
Synchronize spectrums and time domain waveforms to correlate RF and time domain events

 Watch our on-demand webinar, where Alan Wolke will showcase real-world demonstrations of the benefits of these measurements across different RF signals with their own distinct settings.
